title: Activation Decay & Escalation Matrix — Scoring Worksheet (v0.3)
content:
Purpose:
This worksheet captures an experimental scoring approach for customers where recent activation has stalled (activation decay) and there is a growing risk that unresolved friction will require escalation. The goal is a lightweight, repeatable score that drives automated runbook decisions and QBR talking points.

Context and motivation:
- We observe a class of accounts that initially adopt features then plateau; early warning signals are subtle but predictive of churn if not escalated.
- This sheet blends product usage signals + support friction + ROI indicators to produce a single, explainable health score and escalation tier.
- Intended to be used by CSMs and the Escalation Triage team as part of weekly risk review.

Scoring summary (high-level):
- Dimensions: Activation (30%), Engagement cadence (20%), Feature coverage (15%), Support friction (20%), Business ROI signal (15%)
- Per-dimension scale: 0 = critical problem / no signal, 1 = weak, 2 = moderate, 3 = healthy/best practice
- Weighted score = sum(weight * dimension_score) / max_possible -> normalized 0..1 -> map to tier

Dimensions and rubrics (workable rules for automation):
1) Activation velocity (weight 0.30)
  - 3: Key onboarding flows completed in first 14 days; mean time-to-first-success < 48h
  - 2: >50% onboarding flows completed; first-success within 3-7 days
  - 1: partial onboarding (25-50% flows); first-success >7 days
  - 0: <25% onboarding flows completed or missing essential setup

2) Engagement cadence (weight 0.20)
  - 3: Weekly active usage and >3 requests/day (or equivalent workload)
  - 2: Bi-weekly activity with 1-3 requests/day
  - 1: Monthly bursts only, <1 request/day average
  - 0: No activity in last 30 days

3) Feature coverage (weight 0.15)
  - 3: Using 4+ core product capabilities (e.g., hosted API + cache + streaming + evaluate)
  - 2: Using 2-3 capabilities and basic integration patterns
  - 1: Single feature usage with limited depth
  - 0: Intended feature not integrated or blocked by technical issues

4) Support friction & reliability (weight 0.20)
  - 3: 0-1 P1/P2 incidents in last 90 days; ticket resolution SLA met; no open blockers
  - 2: 2-3 incidents or one unresolved medium-priority technical blocker
  - 1: Repeated P2s or P1 >24h active incident within 30 days
  - 0: Ongoing P1 >48h or multiple escalation threads open with no owner

5) Business ROI signal (weight 0.15)
  - 3: Clear usage tied to revenue or product milestone; exec sponsor engaged; renewal >80% likely
  - 2: Early ROI signs (lead indicator), sponsor involved occasionally
  - 1: Unclear ROI; value metrics flat or declining
  - 0: No path to ROI identified or cancelled pilots

Mapping and thresholds (normalized score S between 0..1):
  - S >= 0.80 -> Green (Healthy) — low touch, standard QBR cadence
  - 0.60 <= S < 0.80 -> Amber (Watch) — CSM to run targeted adoption play; recommend micro-QBR
  - 0.40 <= S < 0.60 -> Red (At-risk) — require escalation prep; open tactical task list; consider Dedicated/Optimization review
  - S < 0.40 -> Critical — Immediate escalation to SE + Solutions Eng; possible executive outreach and renewal risk flagged

Example calculation (fabricated account: AcmeRetail Inc):
  - Activation velocity = 2 (weight 0.30) -> 0.6 contribution
  - Engagement cadence = 1 (0.20) -> 0.2 contribution
  - Feature coverage = 2 (0.15) -> 0.30 contribution
  - Support friction = 1 (0.20) -> 0.20 contribution
  - Business ROI = 1 (0.15) -> 0.15 contribution
  - Weighted sum = 0.6 + 0.2 + 0.30 + 0.20 + 0.15 = 1.45 out of max 3.00 (since each dimension max = weight*3 -> total max 1.0*3?)
  - Normalize: divide by (sum of weights*3) = 3.0 so S = 1.45 / 3.0 = 0.483 -> Red band (At-risk)
  - Immediate recommended next steps: schedule deep-dive with engineering + create 30-day remediation plan; open ticket CS-ACME-124; demo advanced features and provide two-week adoption checklist

Operational runbook (action tied to tier):
  Green (>=0.8): automated monthly health email + product tips; archive adoption playbook notes
  Amber (0.6-0.79): assign 1-week micro-play (targeted onboarding nudges, eval tests); track progress in CS tracker
  Red (0.4-0.59): 3-step escalation: (1) CSM triage and 7-day action items, (2) Solutions Eng consult within 48h, (3) weekly check-ins until S >0.6
  Critical (<0.4): immediate SE + SRE triage; legal/CSM to flag renewal; exec sponsor outreach within 72h

Escalation prioritization matrix (tie-breakers when multiple accounts in Red/Critical):
  1) ARR at risk (higher ARR = higher priority)
  2) Upcoming renewal within 90 days -> bump priority
  3) Strategic / reference customers -> bump priority
  4) Number of unresolved P1/P2 incidents

Sheet layout suggestion (columns for spreadsheet ingestion):
  - account_id, account_name, owner, last_activity_date, onboarding_completion_pct, activation_score, cadence_score, coverage_score, friction_score, roi_score, weighted_raw_sum, normalized_score, tier, next_actions, escalation_owner, notes

Sample rows (CSV style):
  1001, AcmeRetail, Rebecca N., 2025-02-04, 60, 2, 1, 2, 1, 1.45, 0.483, Red, "SE deep-dive + 30d plan", Marco Ruiz, "Waiting on SSO fix"
  1002, BrightDistro, Marco R., 2025-01-28, 85, 3, 3, 3, 3, 2.38, 0.793, Amber, "Push feature adoption emails", Elena Brooks, "Pilot launched; latency fine"

Notes on calibration and pitfalls:
- Weighting matters: we chose Activation as highest because initial momentum is highly predictive for this cohort; for upsell-driven accounts you may want ROI heavier.
- Watch for double-counting signals (e.g., support tickets may depress both friction and cadence) — prefer primary attribution rules.
- Periodically calibrate thresholds with actual renewal outcomes (A/B test for 6 months).
- Automation tips: compute scores daily; only surface accounts with S < 0.6 to triage queue.

Open questions / follow-ups for team:
- Agree on ARR threshold tiers for escalation tie-breakers (suggest: <100k, 100-1M, >1M)
- Confirm which onboarding flows map to "key flows" (product to own list)
- Should we include sentiment from support chats as a separate micro-signal?

Immediate next steps (owners and timeline):
- Rebecca: finalize onboarding-flow definitions (due 2024-11-21)
- Marco: wire up ETL from product metrics to sheet prototype (due 2024-12-05)
- Elena: draft escalation email templates for Red/Critical tiers (due 2024-12-12)

Appendix / quick cheat sheet (for CSMs):
- If S < 0.6 -> start a 7-day adoption sprint and copy Solutions Eng into the ticket
- If open P1 >24h -> escalate to SRE and flag for exec update if customer ARR > 250k
- Use the CSV layout above to bulk upload into CS tracker; keep notes concise and time-stamped

Revision history:
- v0.1 (2024-10-15): initial idea and basic rubric
- v0.2 (2024-11-07): added ROI signal and escalation matrix; migrated to sheet format
- v0.3 (2025-02-12): adjusted weights after pilot; added normalization example and tie-breaker rules
